# Experiment runbook

These recipes are based on the checked-out upstream tree. Verify each binary's --help and --list-devices on the host; device names are examples. Hardware qualification is pending.

## Phase 0 — Before cards

Run planner tests and all four example JSONs. Review failure cases: total capacity insufficient, an individual layer too large, duplicate physical card aliases, too little workspace/KV reserve. The bounded PyRe source map is in 04_PYRE_INTEGRATION. If further discovery is needed, pass explicit narrow roots and a harness-owned output directory to audit_local_projects.ps1; the README gives that scoped recipe. Map the current scheduler before editing it. Preserve CPU fallback and durable run records.

Inspect upstream docs/build.md, docs/multi-gpu.md, docs/backend/SYCL.md and tools/rpc/README.md in repos/llama.cpp. All commands are tied to records/repositories.json; updating a repository requires revalidating flags and RPC compatibility.

## Phase 1 — One card, one backend

Record exact GPU SKU/VRAM, physical PCI ID, OS, firmware, driver, runtime/compiler and executable hash. Enumerate devices in the chosen runtime and verify negotiated PCIe speed/width under load. Compare a small workload against CPU numerical reference before capacity scaling. Baseline the current 5070 Ti separately; its relocation can change performance.

Requirements: current vendor driver; CMake/C++ toolchain; backend libraries. Windows native and Linux are separate qualification targets. WSL adds another compatibility layer and cannot be assumed to match native multi-GPU behavior.

## Build recipes

From repos/llama.cpp; install backend prerequisites from the upstream docs first.

```text
# Common API, any vendor with supported Vulkan features/operations
cmake -S . -B build-vulkan -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build-vulkan --config Release -j 4

# NVIDIA native, CUDA toolkit required
cmake -S . -B build-cuda -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build-cuda --config Release -j 4

# AMD native; Linux example, replace target with actual architecture
cmake -S . -B build-hip -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=<actual-gfx-target> -DGGML_RPC=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build-hip --config Release -j 4

# Intel native; source oneAPI environment first, Linux example
cmake -S . -B build-sycl -DGGML_SYCL=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx -DGGML_SYCL_F16=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build-sycl --config Release -j 4
```

Windows HIP needs its own Ninja/clang/architecture setup from upstream. Windows SYCL can use upstream win-build-sycl.bat or matching released packages. The recipes do not install drivers or promise that one toolchain can build every backend in one process. Use separate build directories and environments.

## Phase 2 — All NVIDIA, all AMD, all Intel

Enumerate first, then use returned names explicitly:

```text
llama-cli --list-devices
llama-cli -m <local-model.gguf> --device <device0>,<device1>,<device2>,<device3> --split-mode layer --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 -ngl 99 -c 2048 -n 64
```

Choose a licensed model whose measured load exceeds one card's usable capacity but fits the predicted sharded plan. Start with a smaller model to prove correctness first. Give unequal cards unequal splits based on actual usable memory and measured stage time. Ratio flags are coarse placement hints, not hard byte limits. Inspect logs and peak allocations.

Test at context 512/2048/8192 if supported, one and several active sequences, then repeated cycles. Compare logits/tensors with explicit tolerances; generated prose alone is weak correctness evidence. Quantization and different kernels may cause small drift. Require all cards to own unique model blocks; duplicated models/CPU offload do not satisfy the single-model VRAM-capacity gate.

Probe directed peer access per pair using CUDA/HIP/Level Zero. Do not force P2P when a runtime rejects it. Run host/device/device transfer benchmarks at 8 KiB, 1 MiB, 64 MiB and larger supported sizes, both alone and concurrently. Include synchronization and host staging. Store bandwidth, latency and correctness checks. Intel compute-benchmarks and AMD TransferBench are included for this purpose; consult their --help and architecture/build support rather than applying them indiscriminately across vendors.

## Phase 3 — Mixed vendors using Vulkan

Use one Vulkan build and choose each physical card once. Check supported operations using test-backend-ops; start with the operator set actually used by the selected model. Repeat the same layer-split experiment and record cross-device host-staging traffic. Reject an unsupported operator, invalid output or repeated fallback that defeats the intended capacity test. Compare against each single-card and same-vendor baseline at the same model/quantization/context/batch settings.

## Phase 4 — Mixed native workers through RPC

Use matching commit builds with RPC enabled. On one Windows host, the provided start_rpc_worker.ps1 selects a device and binds to loopback. Example invocations after discovering actual backend names:

```powershell
.\scripts\start_rpc_worker.ps1 -Binary 'E:\the_harness\repos\llama.cpp\build-cuda\bin\Release\ggml-rpc-server.exe' -Device CUDA0 -Port 50052
.\scripts\start_rpc_worker.ps1 -Binary 'E:\the_harness\repos\llama.cpp\build-hip\bin\Release\ggml-rpc-server.exe' -Device ROCm0 -Port 50053
.\scripts\start_rpc_worker.ps1 -Binary 'E:\the_harness\repos\llama.cpp\build-sycl\bin\Release\ggml-rpc-server.exe' -Device SYCL0 -Port 50054
.\scripts\start_rpc_worker.ps1 -Binary '<fourth-card backend RPC binary>' -Device '<fourth distinct physical GPU>' -Port 50055
```

ROCm0 is an example; use the actual name. In another terminal:

```text
llama-cli --rpc 127.0.0.1:50052,127.0.0.1:50053,127.0.0.1:50054,127.0.0.1:50055 --list-devices
llama-cli -m <local-model.gguf> --rpc 127.0.0.1:50052,127.0.0.1:50053,127.0.0.1:50054,127.0.0.1:50055 --device <four returned-RPC-device-names> --split-mode layer --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 -ngl 99 -c 2048 -n 64
```

Select only RPC names so coordinator native aliases do not double-count cards. Confirm startup memory/CPU footprint. Workers must own tensor computation; four whole-model chat servers are a task pool. The fourth worker can use any qualified backend, but must map to a fourth unique physical card. The three named vendor devices are examples, not measured identifiers.

## Windows installed-device smoke — 2026-10-04

The current host has NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti plus AMD gfx1036 integrated graphics, not four purchased discrete cards. Existing Python has Torch CUDA, CuPy, NumPy and PyOpenCL. No driver/toolkit installation is required for this fixture:

```powershell
python .\j_link\opencl_smoke.py
python .\j_link\opencl_smoke.py --inject-corruption
```

Default runs both AMD-to-NVIDIA and NVIDIA-to-AMD pipelines at 32, 2,048 and 262,144 FP32 elements (largest buffer 1 MiB). Source kernel computes 2*x+1, an explicit host NumPy copy bridges separate contexts, and destination kernel computes 3*x-2. CPU reference is 6*x+1. The corruption command must return FAIL/exit 1; ordinary runs return PASS/exit 0 only on measured parity. Missing pairs return NOT_CHECKED/exit 2.

This is EXPLICIT_HOST_STAGED compute/transfer plumbing. AMD reported memory is shared host memory, not dedicated discrete VRAM. Single smoke timings are not bandwidth/performance qualification. Intel, direct peer DMA and four-card inference are not established.

`--probe-invalid-context` is an optional isolated negative control. This machine's attempted cross-platform single-context creation caused native access violation 0xC0000005; this is a real driver/runtime failure, not a clean API rejection. It is not repeated by default. See immutable OpenCL result records. All probe children have bounded supervision.

The retained `j_link/vulkan_smoke.cpp` also passed a 256 KiB NVIDIA-to-AMD transfer. It uses GPU fill/copy commands and forwards the actual NVIDIA readback through host memory; it does not test compute shaders. The accepted build used VS 18, verified official Vulkan headers in `records/vendor_headers/vulkan_1.4.321/include`, and the import library derived from this host's existing loader in `records/vulkan_smoke_20261004/sdk_link`. Build and run records, including the failing corruption control, are in `revision_3`. Preserve the internal 10-second fence deadline and separate 60-second process supervision when rerunning.

`j_link/d3d12_smoke.cpp` passed a different 256 KiB path: an explicit shared cross-adapter heap, placed buffer resources on NVIDIA/AMD, and a GPU cross-adapter fence handoff. All bytes matched; injected corruption failed at byte 12,345. See `records/d3d12_smoke_20261004/placed_heap_revision/receipt.md` and its VS 18/SDK 10.0.26100 build wrapper. The API requires L0 system memory; returned heap descriptors were recorded, physical residency was not measured. This is not dedicated-VRAM P2P. The earlier committed-buffer E_INVALIDARG is a preserved implementation failure, superseded by this working legal API path. Keep the 10-second completion and 60-second process limits.

Four actual CPU-backed RPC workers also passed the current `j_link/rpc_four_worker_smoke.cpp` fixture. Its four stages and three tensor transfers prove CPU/RPC plumbing only. Windows out-of-source build, commands, output and cleanup are in `records/rpc_four_worker_20261004`. This does not qualify the CUDA/HIP/SYCL/Vulkan worker builds described above.

## Working neural execution experiment

The retained `j_link/opencl_executor.py` runs a deterministic eight-layer FP32 residual MLP across the installed NVIDIA/AMD pair. Each owner uploads its unique assigned weights once before inference; its activations stay in device buffers between local layers. Actual GPU activation bytes cross the vendor boundary through host memory. CPU reference states derive independently from the original input. Each layer's full tensor is compared, and GPU events, weight hashes, ownership and transfer counters are recorded.

```powershell
python -B -m unittest discover -s j_link/tests -v
python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --output records/my_fresh_mlp_default.json
python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --reverse --output records/my_fresh_mlp_reverse.json
python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --inject-corruption --output records/my_fresh_mlp_corruption.json
python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --policy-mib 1
python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --device-ids p9:d9
```

Use fresh result paths to preserve previous receipts. Normal and reversed runs require PASS/exit 0. The corruption run must execute the remaining GPU layers, produce a measured final-reference mismatch, report its negative control as detected, and return FAIL/exit 1. Budget refusal is REFUSED/exit 2; a missing device is NOT_CHECKED/exit 2. No runtime discovery or execution happens outside the parent's 60-second child supervisor. The test suite exercises admission before native allocation with mocks; absence of counters in a denial receipt is not a measured zero-allocation result.

The installed pair passed all eight kernels and CPU comparisons in both orders, maximum final absolute error `8.344650268554688e-06` at `atol=rtol=5e-5`. All eight corruption kernels executed; the last four stage comparisons and final parity failed, final error `1.001207709312439`. This is an actual small neural execution result. It is not a GGUF/attention/KV/LLM result, and the AMD device uses shared host memory. See `records/J_LINK_ACCEPTANCE_20261004.md` and `records/opencl_executor_20261004/final_revision/receipt.md` for the final source and logs.

## Integrated four-card release test

These are proposed qualification steps, not completed hardware results. Freeze counts, durations and component-specific limits in a run manifest before executing; preserve failed receipts rather than rerunning until one appears green.

1. Freeze source, binaries, model hashes, OS/drivers and card SKUs. Map A–D to four unique physical GPUs and receiver links. Record dedicated capacity, observed free memory and measured peak allocations per card. Keep the host/display 5070 Ti separate from this four-card result; exclude AMD integrated shared memory from purchased VRAM totals.
2. Qualify the small computation on all four cards first. Supply four independently discovered runtime IDs to the command below, then repeat with `--reverse` and, for mixed vendors, `--inject-corruption`. Require every card to own unique resident layers, actual completed kernels on all owners, independent tensor parity, and correct host-staging counters. Repeat the same width/layers/policy with only three IDs and require modeled capacity refusal. Same-vendor corruption is refused because this control specifically targets a vendor boundary.

   ```text
   python -B j_link/opencl_executor.py --device-ids <A> <B> <C> <D> --width 512 --batch 8 --layers 16 --policy-mib 9 --output <fresh-result.json>
   ```

   This demonstrates modeled blocks of 32 MiB versus three 8 MiB layer budgets. Actual weights total only `16,809,984` bytes. Bounds of width 512, sixteen layers, policy 64 MiB and combined model buffers below 32 MiB deliberately prevent an 8 GB physical-capacity test.
3. Establish real capacity with a separate qualified model runtime. Use a hashed licensed local model, fixed quantization/context/batch and supported operators. Its measured unique device-resident requirements must exceed the largest single card's usable dedicated memory while fitting the four-card plan. Require the identical one-card configuration to refuse capacity and the four-card configuration to pass, with no CPU layer/offload fallback or whole-model replication. To prove that the fourth card is necessary, additionally choose a measured workload exceeding the three-card usable budget and verify three-card capacity refusal. Do not substitute planner estimates, output prose or artificial policy caps for these measurements.
4. Qualify required operations and directed transfers on the pinned runtime builds. Capture tensor/logit tolerance, peak memory, actual transport, latency and throughput against single-card and same-vendor baselines. Use only returned physical/backend or RPC device names. Four CPU workers do not satisfy this gate.
5. Exercise bounded failure controls before extended loading. Stop one owned RPC worker while an inference is active, cancel a coordinator run, request a policy refusal, and exercise allocator failure through a mock or isolated small allocation fixture; never deliberately exhaust the desktop's shared memory. Require explicit failed state, no partial-success receipt, owned-process/port cleanup and release of leases. Restart from a documented committed boundary and verify which state is replayed. This small executor has no durable restart or worker-recovery contract; those tests remain future integration requirements.
6. Qualify the actual integrated core and electrical path. Measure PSU/receiver/connector/fastener geometry and removal paths; print fit/load coupons before the continuous core. Record component masses, supported overhang, total printed mass, actual cable bends, simultaneous startup/load and connector/support temperatures. Require four links to remain stable under simultaneous computation. A proposed initial sequence is twenty cold-start/load/cleanup cycles followed by a two-hour steady mixed load, with logs sampled every second. Stop on a parity error, link reset, connector damage, unsafe measured temperature or a component's documented limit. These durations are test-design choices, not completed endurance results; select thermal/load thresholds from the final components and filament data before testing.

## Qualification matrix and pass conditions

| Gate | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Discovery | Stable physical identity; no duplicate backend aliases |
| Allocation | Measured peak per-device use; reserved space; no double-counted shared host memory |
| Larger model | Unique weight/KV ownership on multiple cards; larger than one card's budget |
| Numerical correctness | Fixed tensor/logit fixtures; tolerance, dtype and quantization recorded |
| Transfer | Directed matrix, sizes, concurrency, synchronization; checksums/parity |
| Useful performance | End-to-end load, prefill, decode, latency and throughput against baselines |
| Failure | Worker exit, OOM and cancellation lead to explicit failed/retryable state |
| Durability | Terminal loss/restart preserves only committed completed work; in-flight replay specified |
| Thermal/electrical | Links stable, connectors/support temperatures qualified, load/stability checks |

A failed worker's KV cache may be lost; never claim transparent session recovery without checkpoints/replay. Reject or retry from a documented boundary. For PyRe admission, the initial release can queue or reduce context rather than crash or pretend unused memory exists.

Use records/benchmark_template.json for future results. Null fields mean unmeasured. Record separately: display card relocation, CPU-root vs chipset path, driver versions, quantization, batch/context/sequence count and software hash. No hardware PASS is implied by CPU planner or RPC smoke tests.

# PyRe GPU and python_gpu integration

## Evidence actually available

The current public PyRe page describes a Windows Python workbench with queues, resource planning and run records. It says acceleration depends on compatible code/hardware and that scripts specify device use. The public guide describes measured transfer-inclusive crossover, parity gating and resource reservation. These are product descriptions, not proof of today's local implementation.

The Library's PYTHON_GPU_MAXIMIZE_OVERVIEW_20260728.pdf describes conservative CPU/accelerator routing, explicit device and per-device VRAM budgets, durable progress, detached resumable runs and warm GPU state. The PDF has malformed content-stream operators; its original bytes are preserved, and extracted text is best effort. The document is historical, not a current source-code audit.

Windows-side source audit on 2026-10-04 identified `E:\JE_Horizon\pyre\pyre-release-source`, HEAD `174c8ae4af10a4163cc039ee3073056e5fcb5cf1`. Current files were read directly; HEAD is provenance, not a claim that the worktree is clean. Source originals and installed PyRe were not modified.

## Audited precursor: what PyRe already provides

Paths below are relative to `E:\JE_Horizon\pyre\pyre-release-source\src\pyre`; line numbers describe this inspection and can drift.

| Responsibility | Current source evidence | Reuse boundary |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA inventory | `hardware.py:158-229` | Identity/free/total telemetry; discovery differs from execution |
| CUDA/ROCm/XPU execution probes | `capability_probe.py:137-190`, `capabilities.py:162-207,362-385` | Bounded interpreter probes and physical-identity matching |
| Controller vendor launch | `controller_adapter.py:83-157,241-305` | Real CUDA/XPU/ROCm branches; one physical device per controller job at `117-140` |
| Scheduling/admission | `controller.py:420-465`, `controller_resources.py:135-155` | Fresh samples, leases and GPU_DEVICE_BUSY; distinct device lanes can run separate jobs |
| Memory budgets/ceilings | `allocation.py:258-280,345-378`, `target_bootstrap.py:49-112` | Measured free bytes/reserve and cooperative framework ceilings; unsupported enforcement refuses |
| Explicit multiple devices | `allocation.py:171-182`, `target_bootstrap.py:52-93` | Exposes/budgets devices for a target implementing its own distribution |
| Mixed backends in one target | `hardware.py:396-409` | Explicit `MIXED_ACCELERATOR_BACKENDS_UNSUPPORTED`; no mixed-vendor shard executor |
| Physical job contract | `controller_protocol.py:110-155`, `controller_resources.py:42-49` | Single backend/device key/reservation; distributed execution needs a new contract |
| Vendor telemetry | `vendor_telemetry.py:16-19,43-90`, `controller_resources.py:242-254` | ROCm/XPU telemetry and configured interpreter adapters |
| Process ownership | `windows_job.py:172-270,345,366,388` | Windows Job Object process-tree containment, drain/termination evidence |
| Durable controller state | `controller_ledger.py:179-180,217,252,470`, `controller.py:55-77` | WAL/FULL commits/hash chain; unknown process trees retain leases |
| Checkpoint/journal/resume | `checkpoint.py:5,81`, `durable_jsonl.py:144,253,289`, `resume.py:306,334` | Identity-bound committed progress; no automatic distributed tensor/KV replay |
| Warm device state | `gpu_context.py:77-128` | Selected CUDA/ROCm/MPS/CuPy context; XPU warm state not implemented here |

Bounded search covered release `src/pyre`, tests and README. No peer/P2P, VRAM pooling or mixed-backend distribution implementation was found within that scope. Source branches establish implementation intent; PyRe hardware execution and its broad suite were not run. Independent harness smoke tests do not certify installed PyRe.

The parallel repair tree `E:\JE_Horizon\impl\PYRE_RELEASE_REPAIR_20260924` exists, but `controller_resources.py` and `target_bootstrap.py` differ from the release tree. Do not mix them. `E:\python-gpu-maximize` is missing; the fresh manifest points to an archived repo shell rather than an active checkout. The older `E:\python_gpu` runner/governor assumes machine-specific CUDA paths/NVIDIA telemetry. Its portable core has CUDA/ROCm/MPS but no XPU. Prefer a coherent current PyRe snapshot.

## Local audit needed

The direct audit above met this session's bounded source scope. `scripts/audit_local_projects.ps1` was inspected rather than run: defaults scan wide roots and write a report. For further discovery, supply narrow roots/output under the harness and read local AGENTS first. Recheck selected files/commits before integration.

Read local AGENTS.md instructions before editing. Map source paths/symbols to responsibilities. Identify whether python_gpu is a still-active dependency, an ancestor or a separate project. Preserve existing behavior and review the local git diff before any integration. The historical overview's flags must not be assumed to remain current.

## Proposed architecture

PyRe owns user-visible scripts, run queue, resource plan approval/selection, durable progress and results. J-Link is an optional service/library behind it: device registry, capability probing, capacity proposals, leases, worker topology and sharded-model execution. Backend workers own runtime allocations and compute.

Start with subprocess/JSON integration and a documented versioned contract. Avoid importing CUDA/HIP/SYCL into the UI process. Keep native environments separate; expose error codes and artifact paths. The first prototype can run entirely as a sidecar under E:\the_harness with no Store application changes.

## Proposed request and response

Request: request_id; mode (task_pool/layer_shard); exact executable/commit; model/workload fingerprint; participating physical device IDs; backend aliases; context/batch/sequence count; precision; per-device peak-memory plan; transfer requirements; timeout; checkpoint policy.

Response: plan_id; selected devices; block ownership; predicted capacity (not speed); source of memory sample; measurement timestamps; leases acquired or refusal reason; launch manifest; run/result IDs. A plan alone is not an allocation guarantee.

Runtime records: leased-but-unallocated bytes, resident bytes, high-water mark, worker heartbeat, topology sample, committed task count, exit status and output parity artifact. GUI capacity labels must distinguish dedicated VRAM, usable allocation budget, host RAM offload and hypothetical capacity.

## Integration sequence

1. Read-only audit and baseline current tests.
2. Add pure planning and JSON serialization behind an optional flag.
3. Add stable discovery/alias mapping and memory snapshots.
4. Implement atomic per-device admission and bounded host buffers.
5. Add one backend/one worker and parity tests.
6. Qualify all-NVIDIA, all-AMD and all-Intel separately.
7. Add mixed Vulkan/RPC experiments with explicit experimental labeling.
8. Add resumable orchestration only at well-defined commit/replay boundaries.
9. Expose measured results in PyRe; keep CPU fallback until crossover proves benefit.

The July goal of being never slower requires an admission/routing policy, not a universal promise about arbitrary scripts. Benchmark end-to-end workload shapes, including process startup, model load, copies and result collection. Do not convert general Python code to GPU code silently.

## Future source review output

Amend this source map with fresh commits/byte hashes, physical acceptance and minimal interface changes before editing PyRe. Reuse identity normalization, byte budgets, admission, ledger/reconciliation, process ownership and checkpoint/journal primitives behind adapters. A distributed J-Link executor still needs partitioning, transport, lifecycle, parity and physical-device acceptance; this audit does not implement it.

# Harness master update

The complete recovered details are in `RECOVERED_CURRENT_COMPLETE.md`; this document provides the reconciled design and additional engineering issues exposed by the software research.

## Mechanical baseline

User-confirmed requirement: **Integrated core; GPU overhang allowed.** Repack all four independently serviceable external bays A–D into one continuous monolithic printed skeleton. Restructure the whole core around the four-card topology; do not append a fourth printed side module to the former three-bay body. Keep all printed bay-support mounts, PSU restraint and fan/plenum hardpoints within that one core. Removable covers, shoes, bolts, metal rails and electronics remain service parts. Another pod still needs a metal joining plate and a separately qualified compute transport.

Recorded printer: Ender-3 S1 Pro, nominal 220 x 220 x 270 mm. Conservative print bounding box: at most 200 x 188 x 254 mm. The recovered installed orientation is 254 W x 200 D x 188 H mm, but it is a starting orientation rather than a fixed prerequisite for Tetris packing. The solver must evaluate installed orientation and print rotation together: the same conservative print box could instead become, for example, 188 W x 200 D x 254 H or 200 W x 188 D x 254 H. Validate every selected rotation with support/brim, full carriage travel and load-direction checks. Printed pillars/rails themselves must stay within the print box; installed cards and outboard PSU may overhang.

The old three-bay width map was 3 x 68 + 2 x 12 + 2 x 13 = 254 mm. Four parallel equal bay allocations require W = 4 t + 62 mm, so a fully contained parallel 68 mm population needs 334 mm. The algebraic 48 mm limit at W=254 applies only to that specific contained parallel arrangement; it is not the new design requirement or a card-selection cap. Retain the original 35–68 mm, 165 mm height and 360 mm length target as a separate universal packing study, alongside actual compact cards. An 8 GB memory specification says nothing about cooler dimensions.

No packing study below establishes a complete chassis fit. Unknown receiver, clamp, base/roof, cable and PSU envelopes can invalidate a promising card-box arrangement. The integrated four-card layout is pre-CAD; no final fit, CAD or production STL is released.

## Integrated Tetris packing studies

Use L x h x t = 199 x 116 x 40 mm for the actual GIGABYTE GV-N5050WF2OC-8GD, and 360 x 165 x 68 mm for the original universal maximum. Bounds below include 13 mm outer margins across the stated pack-width axis and 12 mm gaps where shown. They exclude base/roof/support thickness, receivers, power/signal connectors and bends, PSU, fans/plenum and removal/tool volumes. They are GPU-only packing arithmetic, not production collision results.

| Candidate | Compact 5050 pack W x D x H, mm | Universal maximum pack W x D x H, mm | Consequence for recovered 254 x 200 x 188 core |
|---|---|---|---|
| Four parallel upright |222 x 199 x 116; W=4 t+36+26 |334 x 360 x 165 | Compact GPU-only fit; universal width extends 80 mm. Retain as comparison, not the sole design |
| **Three upright + one rolled 90 degrees about its length, above** |170 x 199 x 168; W=3 t+24+26, H=h+12+t |254 x 360 x 245 | Compact GPU-only fit leaves 84 W/1 D/20 H before unknown interfaces. Universal extends 160 D and 57 H; overhang is allowed but integrated supports remain unqualified |
| Two upright columns x two upright tiers |118 x 199 x 244; W=2 t+12+26, H=2 h+12 |174 x 360 x 342 | Height exceeds recovered core by 56/154 mm. Two 165 mm layers do not fit 188 H |
| Two flat columns x two flat tiers |270 x 199 x 92; W=2 h+12+26, H=2 t+12 |368 x 360 x 148 | Width exceeds recovered core by 16/114 mm. Turning long axis across W trades width for depth: compact 199 W x 270 D x 92 H with margins on D |
| Two lanes, two opposed cards per lane |118 x 410 x 116; D=2 L+12 |174 x 732 x 165 | Central integrated support with front/rear projection; center receivers/service space can require greater D. Large stability and access burden |
| Four upright 90-degree pinwheel, conservative square arrangement |277 x 277 x 116; square side=L+t+12+26 |466 x 466 x 165 | Orthogonal rotation alone is not a contained fit; installed overhang and support poses must be solved |

Prioritize the three-upright-plus-one-flat topology in the parametric search. Card D needs the core's own reinforced pillars/crossmembers and a qualified metal support rail where required. It must never rest on cards A–C, their shrouds/fans, or the PCIe connector. Rotate D's receiver/bracket datum 90 degrees with the card. Model independent removal of every card, including whether lower cards can exit without removing D. Its intake/exhaust direction and the clear 12 mm gap are hard constraints.

For the universal 3+1 pack, 245 H exceeds the recovered 188 H installed orientation. A tall installed orientation with 254 H leaves only 9 mm beyond the GPU-only 245 H before floor/roof/receiver allowances. Its 188 W or 200 W core is narrower than the 254 W lower pack: that pack would extend 66 mm or 54 mm in total, respectively (33/27 mm per side if centered). Card overhang is authorized; printable support footprints, receiver datums, bracket restraints and load paths within the narrower core are not yet proven. An upper support contact can be below the card's top, but its location cannot be invented from an outer box. No orientation alone proves this layout fits.

The two 120 mm fan frames require 240 mm across the recovered fan wall; a 170 mm compact GPU pack can still use a 254 W core. A narrower/taller core needs a re-solved fan placement, not an automatic reuse of that fan wall. If 25 mm fan thickness and 25–35 mm plenum lie serially ahead of a 199 mm card, their GPU/fan/plenum depth is 249–259 mm, requiring 49–59 mm installed rear projection beyond 200 D before other clearances. The compact 3+1 pack's 1 mm depth and 20 mm height remainders are bottlenecks, not spare integration room. PSU body, restraint, airflow and connector reserves must be modeled explicitly.

### Next CAD packing constraints and gates

1. Keep one connected printed support skeleton within 200 x 188 x 254 mm in its selected print rotation. Search card orientation, translation, receiver/bracket poses and installed core rotation jointly; no appended bay-D print and no fixed 48 mm thickness cap.
2. Treat each card, receiver PCB/underside, connector straight zone, cable bend, safe support patch, clamp, fan sweep/plenum, PSU/air keepout and tool region as a separate solid or constraint. Unknown measured interfaces remain unresolved, never zero-volume obstacles.
3. Check installed static collisions and swept independent-removal volumes. Preserve 12 mm intake throats after every interface intrudes. Longitudinal staggering saves width only where card bodies actually cease overlapping; moving a bracket plane alone cannot remove a cooler collision.
4. Constrain every support footprint to the one core; evaluate overhang spans, center of gravity, tip stability, metal reinforcement, layer direction and PETG creep. All four cards transfer load through safe supports/brackets to reinforced rails and feet.
5. Rank feasible poses by installed footprint, access, intake/exhaust compatibility, connector bends, load spans and print mass. Card-box compactness alone is not the objective.
6. Release only after measured GPU/receiver/PSU datums, collision/removal checks, print/brim/support fit, coupons, spool report and simultaneous four-card thermal/load tests. Preserve preferred <=3 kg and hard <=4 kg total on one fresh continuous 5 kg spool. Unknown gates keep this a concept; no CAD/STL issuance from these calculations.

Cards over the original 1.2 kg target need a metal tail support; the original maximum with that support is 2.2 kg. Both targets require qualification. Four-card totals are 4.8/8.8 kg before PSU and other components; these are test loads, not certified chassis ratings.

Primary GPU load goes into padded body supports and bracket restraints, then reinforced rails/feet. Do not let the PCIe socket carry the card's mass. Every bay must allow independent removal. Avoid pressure on fans, heatpipes, components and connectors. Provide a stable footprint including any PSU or card overhang; perform a tip/stability check with the heaviest population.

## Printing and material

Baseline: plain PETG on one continuous 5 kg spool, external bearing holder, 0.6 mm nozzle, approximately 0.28 mm layers after calibration. Preferred total slicer mass <=3 kg; hard planning ceiling <=4 kg including support/brim. A multi-pack of 1 kg spools does not meet the continuous-spool requirement.

Use ribs, gussets, fillets, open windows and box sections. Remove material from broad cosmetic skins, cover fields and plenum panels first. Preserve receiver rails, GPU brackets, PSU strap anchors, fan bosses, feet, docking bosses and strain-relief anchors. Local perimeter/infill guidance is preserved in the recovered print plan. Numbers are starting profiles, not strength certification.

Printing in the recorded tall orientation needs a layer-direction load review after the part is rotated. Reinforce junctions exposed to layer separation. PETG creep means broad metal washers/spacers and modest clamp pressure. Qualification uses conservative printed-support temperature limits in the originals; change material/process if the load paths become too warm or compliant.

## Fasteners

M4 through-bolts, washers and metal nuts for primary structure; M3 metal standoffs and machine screws for boards. Secondary lids/controllers can use measured heat-set inserts. No structural self-tapping screws into PETG.

Original stocking quantities and lengths are preserved in FASTENERS_AND_HARDPOINTS. They are purchase allowances plus spares, not a final assembly count. Final CAD must produce actual stack thickness, thread engagement, nut/tool access and installed quantities. Select fan screws only after fan/guard/pad/boss/washer stack is modeled. Do not substitute arbitrary metric screws into GPU I/O brackets or PSU factory threaded holes; use the designed clamp/strap or confirm their actual thread.

## Air and cable paths

Two 120 mm pressure fans and a 25–35 mm common plenum remain an unqualified candidate for four bays. Recorded P12 Max envelope: 120 x 120 x 25 mm, hole centers 105 x 105 mm. Preserve open rear exhaust and each card's intake direction. Provide four bay intake paths and at least 12 mm clear separation on the actual neighboring intake faces; label channels from the chosen topology rather than assuming a linear AB/BC/CD row. Requalify distribution and simultaneous four-card thermals; free-air CFM is not chassis airflow. Adding a fan does not itself prove the revised plenum fits or cools correctly.

Separate signal, GPU power and control corridors. Starting minima: signal 28 x16 mm, power 28 x 20 mm per bay, control 14 x 10 mm. Add bay-D receiver/retention, power path, signal lead, service access and strain relief; enlarge shared trunks for four actual cable bundles. Provide connector straight/service zones and vendor bend radii, accessible latches and removable covers. No cables in fan sweep or minimum air channels. Label POD1-A/B/C/D, GPU-A/B/C/D, LINK-A/B/C/D and PWR-A/B/C/D consistently with persistent device IDs.

## PCIe architecture

E1 x16 splits into four CPU-root x4 branches: all four for receivers A–D, with none reserved. Use a matched bifurcation host adapter, four qualified external links and four independently powered mechanical-x16 receivers. Candidate transport remains RIITOP quad OCuLink + ADT F9Q-BK10. Gen4 x4 is the target; an x16-shaped socket is not x16 electrical bandwidth. The separate 5070 Ti needs a mechanically/electrically qualified E4 riser/support route and measured bandwidth. M2_3 shares the E4 lane resource. Current discovery reports the NVIDIA card at x16 before redistribution; do not claim this proposed E4 relocation is already installed or retains that bandwidth.

At PCIe Gen4, x4 signaling payload after 128/130 encoding is about 7.88 GB/s per direction before transaction/software overhead (16 GT/s x 4 x 128/130 / 8). This is a calculated ceiling, not a transfer benchmark. A GPU-to-host-to-GPU copy uses both endpoint links, host memory and driver synchronization; measured transfer can be lower. Chipset devices also share upstream resources. J-Link must keep topology in the placement model.

Final receiver PCB mounts stay slotted until official CAD or caliper measurement supplies hole centers, underside components, connector heights and slot datum. Both published CAD links failed during this collection. Do not treat the archived filename as evidence that CAD was actually downloaded.

## Power sizing using the requested headroom

Let Pload = sum of selected GPU maximum board powers + local fans/control + non-overlapping receiver/conversion losses. GPU board power generally already includes PCIe-slot contribution: do not add another 75 W per card on top without identifying a separate load. For a separate pod PSU, do not include host CPU load if the host has its own PSU.

Two common meanings of 20% headroom:

- 20% above calculated load: rating >=1.20 x Pload.
- Keep 20% of rating unused: rating >=Pload/0.80 =1.25 x Pload.

Planning examples only; 8 GB does not determine board power:

| Four-card illustrative board power +40 W overhead | Pload | Rating >=1.20 x load | Rating >=load/0.80 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 x 130 W | 560 W | 672 W | 700 W |
| 4 x 170 W | 720 W | 864 W | 900 W |
| 4 x 300 W | 1,240 W | 1,488 W | 1,550 W |

These are calculations, not a PSU or GPU purchase recommendation. Exact board limits, four receiver inputs, native cable inventory, transients and derating determine selection. Host CPU/display-card load belongs to the separate host power domain unless that architecture is explicitly revised. Do not double-count fan/receiver overhead already included in Pload.

Use native cables approved for the exact PSU; never mix modular cable pinouts. Map receiver power and GPU auxiliary power separately. Keep independent PSU DC outputs separate. Qualify startup/shutdown sequencing with host off during cable changes; OCuLink hot plug is not assumed. No energized rewiring.

## Expansion and production release

Recorded docking interface: four M4 fasteners on an 80 x 60 mm rectangle, reinforced bosses and a metal plate. A control link is not a PCIe data uplink. All four E1 branches are now consumed; a second pod needs extra root-port capacity, a qualified active switch or another host/network transport.

Production STL requires: exact components; four-card interference and independent removal; four link/receiver enumeration and separate display-route qualification; power/connector map; nut/tool access; stability/load review; printed coupons; bed/brim/support fit; slicer mass; simultaneous four-card airflow/thermal tests. No production STL is included because these inputs are unknown. The recovered Astra handoff describes three bays; apply this four-bay amendment before any new parametric concept model.

Use the integrated release sequence in `03_EXPERIMENT_RUNBOOK.md` to connect these mechanical gates to actual four-card computation and failure controls. Fit coupons must reproduce receiver hole/slot/underside datums, D's rotated receiver, safe card support contacts and fastener/tool clearances. Test PETG pillar/rail coupons under sustained load at the planned support temperature, with measured deflection and layer separation criteria fixed in advance. Calculate tipping/overhang moments using actual card and PSU masses, then verify each card's independent removal sweep. A GPU-box packing result cannot release the core while those interfaces are null.
